units.function: Central access application service for Company human/Agent memberships, permission grants, Owner invariants, instance-admin roles, Company access assignment, human offboarding with open-Work reassignment, role-default compatibility and Company-import membership copying.
units.dependencyDirection: The service directly orchestrates Drizzle membership/grant/instance-role/Issue tables, HTTP conflict errors, Agent assignability, AuthorizationService and compatibility grant helpers. Routes, import/bootstrap and other services call this mutable façade; authorization decisions flow onward to a separate policy service.
units.keyDataModels: CompanyMembership keyed by Company/principal type/principal ID with role and lifecycle status; PrincipalPermissionGrant with permission key, opaque JSON scope and grantor user; InstanceUserRole; Issue assignee/run-lock fields; board/user/agent AuthorizationActor and Company resource.
units.lifecycle: Memberships may be ensured, updated, suspended or archived; permissions are replacement sets or individual upserts; active human Owners are row-locked before selected demotion/archive paths; archival clears grants and reassigns open Issues, resetting in-progress execution pointers; instance admins and cross-Company access are managed separately; import copies active human memberships and derives default grants.
units.testAssessment: The already-audited 509-line embedded-Postgres suite covers important intended behavior, but the implementation exposes serious untested paths. setPrincipalPermission calls ensureMembership with role=member/status=active, and ensureMembership overwrites any differing existing role/status, so granting one permission can silently demote an Owner or reactivate a suspended/archived principal without last-Owner checks. ensureMembership and setUserCompanyAccess independently bypass the locked Owner invariant; setUserCompanyAccess reads its snapshot before the transaction, has a dead last-Owner branch after an earlier blanket Owner/admin rejection, and does no row locking. setMemberPermissions can grant to suspended/archived members. Archival clears Issue execution pointers without coordinating cancellation or fencing an active external Run. Lists are unpaginated, mutable methods do not emit immutable audit/evidence, and English conflict text is the effective error contract.
units.designRationale: Unify human and Agent access around principal membership plus explicit grants, preserve one human Owner, archive rather than delete history, and keep unfinished Work assigned during offboarding while allowing legacy/import compatibility.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a first-class Principal/Employment/Authority lifecycle in which human accountability, Agent authorization, offboarding, Work transfer, active execution fencing and evidence are coordinated without conflating display roles with effective permissions.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT behind OrganizationPrincipal, AuthorizationPolicy, ResponsibilityTransfer, ExecutionControl and Audit ports. Preserve the useful concepts—human/Agent principal union, explicit Company membership, last-accountable-owner invariant, soft archival, scoped grant provenance and non-retroactive historical assignee—but use one invariant-preserving command path, database constraints/serializable locking, monotonic membership versions, stable decision/error codes, deny/expiry/conditions, separation of duties, transfer acceptance, session/secret/runtime revocation and atomic outbox evidence. Route compatibility/import through explicit migration commands, never through normal authority mutation APIs.
units.responsibilityConflict: Permission enablement can silently change role/status and defeat the last-Owner guarantee. Offboarding reassigns Work without acceptance by the new accountable human and can erase active execution pointers without cancelling/fencing the real executor. Company import reproduces authority without target-side identity rebinding or consent. Instance-admin and grant mutations carry no immutable authorization decision/evidence receipt, and arbitrary JSON scope has no typed data/authority semantics.
